title: Day by Day the Manna Fell
description: Day by Day the Manna Fell in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Josiah Conder wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 30, “"Give Us Our Daily Bread."”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Day by day the man-na fell; O, to learn this les-son well! Still by con-stant mer-cy fed, Give us, Lord, our dail-y bread.

lines: Day by day the manna fell;
O, to learn this lesson well!
Still by constant mercy fed,
Give us, Lord, our daily bread.
"Day by day," the promise reads;
Daily strength for daily needs;
Cast foreboding fears away;
Take the manna of to-day.
Lord, our times are in Thy hand;
All our sanguine hopes have planned
To Thy wisdom we resign,
And would mould our wills to Thine.
Thou our daily task shalt give;
Day by day to Thee we live;
So shall added years fulfil
Not our own, our Father's will.
O, to live exempt from care,
By the energy of prayer;
Strong in faith, with mind subdued,
Glowing yet with gratitude!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Josiah Conder died in 1855.
credits: Words by Josiah Conder (1789–1855), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
